The WHO and ministry assessment of September 2022 states that the Federal Ministry of Health runs the national HMIS on DHIS2 from its own data centre with a cloud-based server, with an HMIS structure connecting district, region, state and federal levels.

The assessment states that strengthening the health information system is entirely dependent on donors, that the Global Fund contracted the University of Oslo to build the HMIS rolled out in 2017, and that this over-reliance fragments the system and weakens ministry leadership (September 2022).

As of September 2022 the assessment counts 641 facilities reporting to DHIS2: 3 national hospitals, 26 regional hospitals, 35 district hospitals, 5 private hospitals, 386 health centres, 140 primary health care units and 46 TB centres, excluding Somaliland.

The assessment states that although DHIS2 allows direct entry, in practice most facilities record on 12 standard paper registries and send monthly summary forms to the district HMIS officer, who enters them into DHIS2; only 30-42% of districts have such an officer (September 2022).

The assessment lists digitalisation of data entry as being piloted at selected health facilities, with no count given, and names digitalising data at facility level as a priority still to be taken to scale (September 2022).

The assessment lists among the weaknesses of the public routine system that there is no electronic medical records system (September 2022); it adds that the private sector uses a variety of health information management software, undescribed.

The assessment states that public facilities record patients on standard paper registries supplied by the ministry, including inpatient and outpatient registers, and that there is no electronic medical records system (September 2022).
With no electronic medical records system in the public sector, the assessment records no primary facility keeping digital patient records (September 2022).
